observations.text: SP, due to an incorrect rotation technique after brakes release, did not execute the take off with the standard T/O airspeed and did not maintain the A/C at the runway centerline, with the result of rotation 4 knots below the standard T/O airspeed, against a zero negative tolerance, and a lateral displacement of 16 ft from the centerline. The IP directed the correction and applied part of the directional inputs to re-establish the take off run. Further practice in take off attitude and directional control on the runway is required.

SP, due to distraction by a secondary cockpit task during a critical phase of flight, did not maintain the A/C at the centerline during the interval take off roll and delayed the L/G and flaps retraction, with the result of a lateral deviation of 15 ft from the centerline and acceleration to 13 knots above the standard T/O airspeed before rotation. The IP intervened on the controls to re-establish the take off path and directed the configuration clean-up sequence.

SP, due to a late and coarse rudder input at brakes release, did not keep the A/C on the runway centerline during the interval take off roll, with the result of a lateral deviation reaching 10 ft, at the limit of the allowed tolerance. The deviation was recognized and corrected with delay, only after the IP's verbal prompt. No intervention on the controls was required.

SP, due to inadequate workload management during the take off phase, did not execute the LINE UP checks without omissions and did not bring the A/C to the proper T/O attitude at the briefed point, with the result of rotation 10 knots above the standard T/O airspeed, at the limit of the allowed tolerance. The omitted After Takeoff Checklist items were completed only after the IP's verbal prompts, and the error was recognized with delay.

SP, due to non-standard power lever handling at brakes release, did not execute the take off with the standard T/O airspeed, with the result of rotation 8 knots above the standard T/O airspeed. The deviation was recognized in a timely manner and corrected during the initial climb, and the A/C was cleaned up without violating the speed limit and without the IP's intervention.

SP, due to distraction from the primary scan while monitoring the leader's position ahead on the runway, did not maintain the A/C at the centerline during the interval take off roll, with the result of a lateral deviation of 8 ft from the centerline. The deviation was self-detected and corrected in a timely manner, and the A/C was brought to the proper T/O attitude and accelerated to the standard climb airspeed without the IP's intervention.

SP executed the interval take off within the desired standards, performing the LINE UP checks without omissions, rotating 4 knots above the standard T/O airspeed and holding the A/C within 4 ft of the runway centerline. Both values, however, remained at the upper edge of the tolerance and the configuration clean-up was initiated later than briefed. Marginal performance for the Training Section - closer airspeed control at rotation is expected to improve over the next sorties.

SP executed the interval take off with exceptional accuracy, holding the A/C within 1 ft of the runway centerline throughout the take off roll and rotating within 1 knot of the standard T/O airspeed. The L/G and flaps retraction and the After Takeoff Checklist were completed in the briefed sequence without violating the speed limit, and the A/C was accelerated and maintained at the proper climb airspeed without any IP's prompt. Above end of block MIF achieved.
